Fusebox now measures how fast each model streams its answers, on the Usage page and the Overview. Claude's Fable weekly limit shows on the overview and counts when choosing an account, and the usage writer loses only the records that fail, logging each one.

## Changes

- **Output speed per model.**
  - The Usage page has an **Output speed by model** card for its range and filters. Each model shows its output speed in tokens a second, time to first token, its share of Fast calls, the change against the period before, tokens out and calls. A model that ran at more than one speed tier gets a row per tier, so Codex Fast and Standard show apart. Below the table, a by-day chart (by month for long ranges) shows the models you pick.
  - The Overview's **Load · last 60 min** has an **Output speed** figure. Its hover lists the busiest models, and clicking it opens the Usage page.
  - Speed is output tokens over the time after generation started, summed over calls, so long answers weigh more. Generation starts at the first content, or at the start of reasoning that streams no text (a Codex reasoning item, a Claude thinking block). Reasoning tokens count as output, so the timed span holds the reasoning too.
  - Not timed: failed and cancelled calls, calls without streamed content or reported output, reasoning with no known start (Gemini and Chat streams, redacted thinking), and answers that arrived in one piece (under 50 ms of streaming, or over 10,000 tokens a second).
  - Calls stored before this release are counted but not timed. Earlier releases recorded only when the first visible content arrived, after any hidden reasoning, so their speed would read too high: up to a third for Opus 5.5.
  - [docs/usage-costs.md](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/blob/v0.16.0/docs/usage-costs.md#output-speed) explains the rule.
- **Claude's Fable weekly limit.**
  - The overview shows it as a "↳ Fable" row under each Claude subscription, and under Claude's combined weekly bar. Running low, the row takes the warning colour from 75% used and the error colour from 95%.
  - Claude's usage endpoint marks the Fable limit `is_active: false` whenever another limit ends sooner, which on Ultra accounts is always the week. Fusebox read that as a retired limit, so every Fable window showed 0%. It now keeps the limit: Fable requests weigh the Fable week when choosing an account, a used-up Fable limit stops Fable on that account, and the combined Fable limit can raise the pooled pace warning.
- **Usage records.**
  - When one record in a batch fails, the writer writes the rest one at a time and loses only the failing record, which it logs with its source, provider and time. Before, the whole batch was lost without a log line. If the database itself is failing, the rest of the batch is lost at once, as before.
  - A call without an output count (an error after the first content) no longer fails its batch.
- **iPhone app 1.2.** The Usage page shows output speed per model, from a server running this release. A read the app cancels itself, such as a pull to refresh during a range change, no longer shows "Canceled" with a Retry button.
- **Build.** Every build, the Docker image included, uses Rust 1.100.0. The Release workflow tests the tag on Linux, macOS and Windows before it publishes.

## Upgrading

- **Database.** The usage database stays on schema 5.
  - The first start adds two tables, `usage_timings` and `usage_speed_rollup`, and four triggers on `usage_entries` that keep the speed totals exact. A background pass then counts the calls already stored, newest first, about 2,000 records every 250 ms; the speed card says so while it runs.
  - v0.15.0 keeps reading and writing the database, and the triggers keep the totals exact meanwhile; the calls it serves are left out of the speed card. `usage downgrade` removes the two tables and their triggers.
- **No new settings.**
- **API changes:**
  - New: `GET /api/usage/speed`, with the usual range and filter parameters. It returns, per provider, model and speed tier, the calls, timed calls, output tokens, streaming time and time to first token, per local day and for the period before.
  - Request log entries carry `speed` (left out when standard) and `stream_ms` (when the call is timed). The minute buckets in `/api/overview`'s `series` carry `timed_output`, `stream_ms` and `speeds`.
- **Pricing.** No price changes.

## Known issue

- **SQLite advisory RUSTSEC-2026-0459 ([#60](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/issues/60)).** Unchanged from v0.15.0: the bundled SQLite is still 3.50.2, and the fix (rusqlite 0.41) made usage inserts about four times slower in testing. It matters only where someone less trusted can write files next to the usage database.

Validation: 1,025 Rust tests (13 ignored), 191 dashboard tests and 59 Python tests passed, with formatting and Clippy; the Release workflow tests the tag on Linux, macOS and Windows. The dependency audit still fails only on the advisory above. Production has run output speed since 13 November 2026, timed from generation start since that evening, and the Fable limits since 10 November. Only the history change (calls stored before this release are counted, not timed) is new here.

[Full comparison with v0.15.0](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/compare/v0.15.0...v0.16.0).
